sentence_stem: She has never travelled abroad, but
correct_completion: she has always wanted to visit Italy.
full_sentence: She has never travelled abroad, but she has always wanted to visit Italy.
acceptable_variants: she has dreamed of going there.
she hopes to go one day.

options.text: so she has been to Italy twice.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts 'has never travelled' and uses 'so', which signals a result rather than a contrast.

options.text: she has travelled to five countries.
options.why_wrong: This directly contradicts 'never', so it cannot continue the sentence stem.

options.text: she has always wanted to visit Italy.
and she has never seen the sea.
options.why_wrong: 'And' adds more information rather than contrasting with the first clause, which 'but' requires.

grammar_focus: Present perfect with 'never' and contrast with 'but'
explanation: After 'but', we need a clause that contrasts with 'has never travelled'. The present perfect 'has always wanted' describes a wish that continues up to now, which fits the contrast. Learners often use a simple past here, but English uses the present perfect when the period of time reaches the present.
translation: Nigdy nie podróżowała za granicę, ale zawsze chciała odwiedzić Włochy.
